difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's proposition at source lines 582-589: exponentiation of cardinals distributes over cardinal addition in the exponent and composes in the exponent. The 19-line proof (591-610) proves both laws by exhibiting explicit bijections rather than by quoting arithmetic of cardinals: for the first law it splits a function defined on the disjoint sum of two cardinals into its two components and claims the splitting map is a bijection onto the product of the two function sets (592-600); for the second law it curries a function of two arguments into a function into a function set and claims the currying map is again a bijection (602-609). The statement records neither the splitting nor the currying, and both bijectivity claims have to be verified on the level of functions.
